name: Community-reported vLLM decode throughput on RTX 5090 (sm_120) under WSL2 with CUDA graphs working, Qwen3-14B AWQ
methodology: SINGLE REPORTER, PARTIALLY SPECIFIED. Hardware and software as stated: RTX 5090 32GB GDDR7 (sm_120 Blackwell), Windows 11 + WSL2 2.7.0 pre-release, Ubuntu 22.04, kernel 6.6.114.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2, CUDA 12.8, driver 581.80, vLLM 0.17.1, model Qwen/Qwen3-14B-AWQ via awq_marlin. CUDA graphs enabled (that is the point of the report). Batch size, prompt length, output length, concurrency and whether the figure is per-request or aggregate are NOT stated in the report - the surrounding benchmark table was not captured. The reporter's own comparisons, same post: ~26% faster than Ollama, and 8x faster than --enforce-eager on the same setup. Treat the figure as an order-of-magnitude datapoint, not a benchmark.
notes:
SINGLE REPORT by Kyzcreig (vLLM issue #37242). The number's value is mainly as evidence that the configuration WORKS, not as a throughput claim: the community consensus was that CUDA graph capture on consumer Blackwell under WSL2 was permanently broken because the dxgkrnl Hyper-V GPU virtualization layer did not support it, and the reporter demonstrated it does - after removing the causes of a boot-time race, not by changing anything GPU-specific. His three fixes are all WSL2/driver-service ordering: remove Tailscale (it intercepts the network at boot and interferes with CUDA init), hard-mask nvidia-cdi-refresh (it probes CUDA devices at boot ~11s and races driver init on Blackwell), and delay any CUDA-using service (e.g. Ollama, ComfyUI) by 45s after boot. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION of the works-claim: commenter SoloRyuken confirms CUDA graph capture working on an RTX 5090 under WSL2 2.6.3 stable with ComfyUI 0.19.x in a CUDA 13.0 container - a different stack, same conclusion. The 8x-vs-eager figure is the operationally important one, since --enforce-eager is the reflex workaround most people settle for. Note the issue was auto-closed by GitHub's stale bot, not by a fix.
